title: Generative machine learning identifies and validates new dual- and tri-phase eutectic compositionally complex alloys
summary: A conditional variational autoencoder generated candidate alloy compositions and an artificial neural network ranked eutectic-forming likelihood. The team experimentally validated previously unreported eutectic compositionally complex alloys across quaternary to senary systems. Reported examples include Al₁₆Cr₁₈Fe₂₄Ni₄₂ with a dual-phase FCC/BCC eutectic lamellar structure and Al₁₁.₃Nb₁₃.₇Co₃₆.₆Cr₈.₂Fe₇.₉Ni₂₂.₃ with a tri-phase FCC/BCC/Laves eutectic structure, supported by XRD, SEM and DSC.
ai_technology: Conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE) and artificial neural network (ANN)
organization: City University of Hong Kong; Shenzhen University

evidence.tested: A conditional variational autoencoder generated candidate alloy compositions and an artificial neural network ranked eutectic-forming likelihood.
evidence.unknown: The authors report five newly identified ECCA compositions across the studied systems; this is one paper-level result, not five records. The entry names two representative experimentally examined compositions. Validation is limited to the reported arc-melted samples and XRD/SEM/DSC characterization; no long-term mechanical performance or application testing is established. The training data were sparse and imbalanced, and dataset filtering was part of the framework.
evidence.ai_role: A CVAE generated candidate compositions conditioned on eutectic/non-eutectic microstructure labels; an ANN trained on composition and thermodynamics-derived descriptors estimated eutectic-forming likelihood and selected generated candidates for experimental validation. Dataset preprocessing with PCA and K-means addressed class imbalance. The ML pipeline directly proposed the compositions whose eutectic structures were examined experimentally.
